subject: Cloud marketplaces unit economics — alignment and next steps
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Haynes <sara.haynes@aws-marketplace.com>, Bhavesh Iyer <bhavesh@cloud-retail.xyz>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:23:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + ask: Cloud marketplaces unit economics (AWS/GCP/Azure) — next steps

Hi Sara / Bhavesh,

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion on how private offers would look across AWS/GCP/Azure for Cloud Retail. Quick recap from our side and three asks so we can map to PO unit prices: 

Recap (short):
- Monthly forecast (first 6 months): 150M tokens steady -> growth to ~300M by month 6 if pilot converts.
- Token breakdown (current estimate): generation ~120M/mo, embeddings ~30M/mo.
- Target economics: Cloud Retail is aiming for a blended target in the range of $200–$350 per 1M generation tokens (they have a stretch target of $150) and $80–$180 per 1M embeddings tokens. They asked us to confirm what we can commit to on a private-offer unit price map and how marketplace fees affect final invoiced rate.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you share the marketplace unit-price mapping template you use for private offers (unit price pre-marketplace cut vs final invoice)?
2) What are the typical marketplace commission / fee layers for AWS vs GCP vs Azure for private offers (percent or flat)?
3) We'll send a draft PO mapping (attached) with our suggested unit prices — could you validate feasibility and call out any listing or billing constraints?

Attachments: redwood_po_map_v1.xlsx (draft unit-price mapping), unit_econ_sample_calcs.csv (simple calc tab).

We'd like to schedule a short alignment call the week of Nov 16 to finalize numbers. Proposed: Tue Nov 17 10:00am PT. Does that work?

Thanks,
Dev
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwoodinference.com


From: Sara Haynes <sara.haynes@aws-marketplace.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Bhavesh Iyer <bhavesh@cloud-retail.xyz>
Cc: aws-mp-pricing@amazon.com
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: Cloud marketplaces unit economics (AWS/GCP/Azure) — next steps

Hi Dev — great speaking yesterday. Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments — I'll work with pricing on the template you requested. A few clarifying Qs before we map numbers across marketplaces:

- Can you split the monthly forecast into committed vs burst (committed MAUs / tokens you want to guarantee under the PO)? Marketplaces treat committed spend differently for private offers.
- For generation vs embeddings: do you expect the same model family or different models (this affects sequence-length distribution and per-token cost assumptions).
- Do you have a target monthly committed spend (range) you want on the PO? that helps us shape tiered unit pricing.

High-level on AWS Marketplace private offers:
- We typically show two numbers: seller unit price (what Redwood sets) and final customer invoice (which includes marketplace fees / taxes). Marketplace fees vary by program and channel — for standard private offers there is often a ~15% marketplace fee that sits on top of the seller unit price, though programs and negotiated arrangements can change that.
- There are also listing and billing constraints we should flag (e.g., minimum billing granularity, invoice cycle).

I'll loop in the marketplace pricing team (cc'd) and share our PO/unit-price template by EOD today. If you can answer the three bullets above, that will speed validation.

Regards,
Sara
Sara Haynes
Partner Pricing, AWS Marketplace

Thanks Sara — answers inline below and spreadsheet attached with a committed/burst split.

Committed vs burst:
- Committed: 100M tokens/mo (generation + embeddings combined) as the base guaranteed commit for the pilot.
- Burst: up to 250M tokens in high months (buffer for promotions/seasonal spikes).

Model split and behavior:
- Generation: primarily the “redwood-xxl-gen” family, average seq length ~420 tokens. Estimated generation tokens = 120M/mo (committed portion 80M, burst 40M).
- Embeddings: a mix of short-context embedding calls, avg ~256 tokens per call, estimated 30M/mo (committed 20M, burst 10M).

Target committed spend (monthly): $35k–$90k depending on unit prices selected.

Unit price targets (what Cloud Retail asked us to aim for):
- Generation (1M tokens): target $250 (acceptable $200–$350), stretch $150
- Embeddings (1M tokens): target $120 (acceptable $80–$180)

Notes: the figures above are Redwood's suggested starting points for negotiation. If marketplaces apply a 15% fee on top of the seller unit price, the final invoice to Cloud Retail will be 15% higher unless the private offer structure absorbs part of that.

Attached: redwood_po_map_v1.xlsx (updated with committed/burst columns), unit_econ_sample_calcs.csv

Proposed meeting still Tue Nov 17 10:00am PT — we'll keep it to 30 minutes and have pricing + finance on the call.

Thanks,
Dev

Subject: Re: Draft PO mapping + legal/finance notes

Hi Marissa / Dev — thanks for the updated docs. Confirming Nov 17 10:00am PT for a 30-minute alignment. Pricing team has reviewed the mapping and we have two quick items to tidy before the call:

1) Marketplace fee treatment: We can offer two paths — (A) Redwood lists seller unit price and buyer is invoiced with the marketplace fee added (pass-through) or (B) Redwood sets an adjusted seller unit price that folds the expected marketplace fee into your list price (seller absorbs). Both are supported but will affect how we show pricing in the AWS console and on invoices. We'll have the exact fee percentages for the SKU-level mapping on the call.

2) PO terms: For private offers we typically see minimum term of 3 months for pilot POs; minimum billing granularity is monthly. We'll validate exceptions but plan around that.

Action items before the call:
- Dev: please upload the final HubSpot deal id to the PO spreadsheet (HubSpot link below) and confirm the final committed token quantity you want the PO to guarantee (we have 100M in the draft).
- Marissa: please confirm whether Redwood prefers to absorb marketplace fees or pass-through so pricing can prepare both scenarios.

DocuSign PO template link: https://www.docusign.com/rooms/ABCD-1234-PO
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567890

See you Tue Nov 17 10:00am PT.

Best,
Sara
